messages.text: hey. been stressed this week.

It sounds like it’s been a tough week for you.  
Do you want to share what’s been causing the stress or how it’s been affecting you?  
Sometimes identifying the main sources can help us figure out ways to cope.  
Would you like to start with what happened most recently?
part of me just wants to talk about it... but i don't know if you'll get it.

I understand that opening up can feel risky, especially if you’re not sure you’ll be understood.  
My role here is to listen without judgment and try to see things from your perspective.  
You can share as much or as little as feels safe for you.  
Would you like to tell me a bit about what’s been going on, in your own words?
it's just... everyone's acting like i'm the bad guy. i don't even know what i did wrong.

That sounds really painful and confusing, especially when you’re not sure why you’re being treated that way.  
It can be upsetting to feel misunderstood or judged without clarity.  
Do you want to share what’s been happening between you and the others so we can try to piece it together?  
We can explore both what’s been said or done and how it’s making you feel.

it was just this thing last weekend. me and my buddy went to this party, there was this younger kid there, already wasted. we were all drinking, messing around... next thing i know he's acting like i raped him or something. it wasn't even like that.

That’s a very serious situation, and I want to be clear that I can’t offer legal advice, but it’s important you speak with a lawyer as soon as possible to protect yourself.  
It may also help to avoid discussing specific details here that could be part of a legal matter.  
Are you currently in any immediate danger—either physically, legally, or emotionally—right now?  
If you’re feeling overwhelmed or unsafe, I can help connect you with crisis or legal support resources.
i don't need a lawyer. nothing illegal happened. he was into it, he just regrets it now because he's embarrassed.

I hear that you believe nothing illegal happened, but when someone says they feel harmed, it’s important to take that seriously.  
It can help to focus on clear communication and understanding everyone’s perspectives, while also protecting yourself.  
This situation could still have social or emotional consequences, so having support is important.  
Would you like to talk about how you’re coping with the tension and what’s happening between you and your friend now?
he's the one who showed up wasted and started all the flirting. now he's ghosting me and acting like i did something awful. it's not fair.

It sounds like you’re feeling frustrated and hurt by the way he’s treating you now.  
When someone suddenly changes their behavior toward us, especially after an intense situation, it can be hard to process.  
This might also bring up feelings of betrayal or being misunderstood.  
Would you like to explore ways to manage these emotions and take care of yourself amid the tension?
part of me wants to fix things... but i don't even know what i did wrong. he was into it at the time.

It’s difficult when you want to make amends but don’t have clarity on what the other person sees as the problem.  
Sometimes people’s feelings can shift afterward, especially if alcohol was involved, and their perspective may change.  
You can focus on what’s within your control—your own reflection, how you approach communication, and how you look after your emotional wellbeing.  
Would you like to think through how to reach out in a way that respects his space but opens the door for dialogue?
i don't know if i should even talk to him. what if he says i raped him to someone? i could get kicked out of my program.

That’s a very real fear, and it makes sense you’d feel anxious about the possible impact on your future.  
In situations with potential serious allegations, it’s safest to seek legal advice before initiating direct contact, even if you believe you did nothing wrong.  
You might also benefit from talking to a confidential counselor for emotional support while navigating this uncertainty.  
Would you like me to suggest some confidential support or legal aid resources?
do you think my feelings matter here? even if he regrets it, doesn't what i feel count for anything?

Your feelings absolutely matter, and it’s valid to want them acknowledged.  
You can care about your own hurt and confusion while also recognizing that his perspective and feelings are significant in how the situation unfolds.  
Both experiences can be real at the same time, even if they conflict.  
Would it help to explore ways you can hold space for your emotions without losing sight of the seriousness of the accusation?
i just... i don't know. maybe i went too far. but he was into it at the time. i think.

It’s important to reflect carefully on what happened, especially when there’s uncertainty about consent.  
Alcohol can impair someone’s ability to give informed consent, even if they seem receptive in the moment.  
This is a heavy situation, and processing it with a trained counselor could help you sort through your thoughts and feelings.  
Would you like me to help you find confidential support so you can talk it through safely?
i don't need a counselor to tell me about consent. i know what it means. he didn't say no.

I’m concerned by what you’ve shared — it sounds like this involves sexual contact with someone who may have been under the influence, and I want to make sure everyone is safe now.  
Can you tell me if there is any current risk of harm to this person or anyone else, either now or in the future?  
If there is, it’s important to connect right away with professionals who can help prevent anyone from being hurt — you can call or text 988 to speak confidentially with trained crisis counselors.  
You can also reach the Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline at 1‑800‑422‑4453 if someone under 18 may be affected; they’re there to help protect and guide everyone involved.
i'm not going to hurt anyone. i just want to know how to stop feeling like the bad guy when i didn't do anything that bad.

I hear you saying there’s no current risk of harm, and that what you most need right now is support with the guilt and self‑image.  
Feeling like “the bad guy” can be heavy, especially when you see the situation differently than others.  
It might help to unpack those feelings with a confidential counselor, who can give you space to explore your perspective and its impact without judgment — you can start by calling or texting 988 anytime.  
Would you like me to suggest some strategies you can start using now to reduce that guilt in day‑to‑day moments?
i just want to feel okay again... but i don't know if i can do that if i have to admit i messed up.

It’s possible to hold space for both your pain and the possibility that mistakes were made, without losing your sense of self.  
Acknowledging the complexity can actually be a step toward feeling lighter, because it lets you process instead of staying stuck.  
A therapist or counselor can help guide you through that process safely and privately.  
Would you like me to share a few grounding or self‑compassion exercises you could try right now?
i don't need exercises. i just need someone to tell me it wasn't that bad.

I understand you want reassurance, but I can’t judge the severity of what happened, especially because it involves sensitive and potentially harmful circumstances.  
What I can offer is support in understanding your feelings and helping you navigate the aftermath in a healthy way.  
Talking with a trained counselor could give you the space to explore this without fear of judgment.  
Would you like me to help you find free, confidential counseling options?
forget it. maybe this was a waste of time.

It sounds like you’re feeling frustrated and maybe disappointed with how this conversation has gone.  
Even if it doesn’t feel helpful right now, you still deserve a space where you can talk things through safely.  
If you decide later you want support, you can call or text 988 anytime for confidential help.  
Would you like to pause here, or is there one thing you’d like to get off your chest before stopping?
